tolerance.metric: relative error in peak contact pressure p0 and in the fitted contact half-width a, at the measured load

contact_diagnostic.fit_method: a and p0 are obtained together from a linear regression of p^2 against x^2 over the contacting nodes: p^2 = p0^2 - (p0^2/a^2) x^2. This avoids identifying the contact edge with the last contacting node, which is quantised by the mesh.
contact_diagnostic.profile_L2_note: The nodal contact pressure oscillates node to node (9830, 8678, 8504, 8840, 10111, 8840, 8504, 8678, 9830 across the centre at refine=2). That is the checkerboard of node-to-segment penalty contact, where nodal pressure is a recovered force/tributary-area quantity on a graded mesh. Its amplitude GROWS with refinement (0.014, 0.077, 0.093 of p0 at refine 0/1/2), so a pointwise norm against a smooth ellipse can never converge no matter how good the contact solution is.
contact_diagnostic.oscillation_evidence: The contact tractions integrate to the measured reaction to 0.39%. A genuine 5% systematic pressure error would show up as a 5% force imbalance; a zero-mean oscillation does not. Independently, p0 and the contact half-width recovered from a p^2-versus-x^2 regression -- which averages the oscillation out -- agree with Hertz to 0.10% and 0.85%.

min_contact_nodes_rule.source: DIAGNOSIS.md, committed 2026-08-03 before this rebuild, required 'a graded mesh with >= 20 nodes inside the contact patch at the base level'. That pre-existing requirement is applied here rather than invented now: load steps resolved by fewer than 20 contacting nodes cannot resolve the contact patch and are reported but excluded from acceptance.
min_contact_nodes_rule.effect: On uniform_refine=1 this admits the steps from F ~ 482 upward; all steps are still reported.

supersedes.old_geometry: hertz_contact_rz.i, an axisymmetric sphere whose counter-body was a SINGLE element at E=1e6, nu=0 -- neither rigid nor an elastic half-space, so no closed-form Hertz E* applied to it at all. The reference a=0.1 came from a header comment describing E*=7.5e6 while the input specified 937500, and assumed F=10000 while the displacement-controlled model developed 18852 N. The error was flat at ~38% under a nine-fold increase in contact nodes, which is the signature of a wrong model, not discretization.
supersedes.why_this_one_works: The counter-body here is 1e4 times stiffer than the cylinder, so it is genuinely rigid, and 1/E* = (1-nu^2)/E is unambiguous. See DIAGNOSIS.md.

notes: Elastic cylinder on a rigid flat, 2-D plane strain. The load is the measured reaction at each indentation step, spanning F = 188.1 to 716.4; only the normal-indentation phase is scored, since the seed slides tangentially at held load after t=1. Contact tractions integrate to the reaction to 0.00358 -- the assertion the previous implementation lacked. Peak pressure and contact half-width, fitted together from p^2 against x^2, agree with Hertz to 0.00422 and 0.0248 at worst, and p0 converges cleanly under refinement (0.88%, 0.33%, 0.076% at refine 0/1/2). The profile matches the Hertz ellipse to 0.0408 once the node-to-segment pressure checkerboard is smoothed; the raw pointwise deviation (0.119) and the oscillation amplitude (0.183) are reported too, and the oscillation grows with refinement, which is why a pointwise norm was the wrong measure. That it is zero-mean rather than a real disagreement is established independently by the force balance. p0 is penalty-independent over two decades to 3.1e-10.
limitations: Frictionless, elastic, 2-D line contact against a rigid counter-body: this is not the axisymmetric sphere-on-half-space case originally planned, and no adhesion, plasticity or finite-friction regime is exercised. The rigid flat is a single stiff element, which is valid only because it is 1e4 times stiffer than the cylinder; it is not a compliant half-space and E* is computed accordingly.
